text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.66% today after a week of sharp declines, as oil markets showed signs of stabilizing following geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. U.S. crude fell nearly 8% last week as Iran and the U.S. held talks at the U.N., but Trump's rejection of Iran's ceasefire proposal on Thursday has shifted expectations back toward escalation and potential supply disruptions, which would support higher oil prices and refinery margins.

The company operates in a complex moment: U.S. oil is trading at $96.41 per barrel while global crude sits at $114.89, a wide spread that reflects Middle East supply fears. Refineries are running at 94% capacity with ample product in storage, so the near-term calculus hinges on whether geopolitical risk will push oil prices higher or whether the ceasefire talks keep them volatile but contained.
